write.title: Start with a sentence.
write.problem: You stop mid-sentence to hunt for an em dash.
write.answer: Every mark a novel needs is one keystroke. The line you're writing stays in view, and the rest of the page steps back.

more.engine: A text engine of its own, built for fiction: its own document model, undo tree and diff.
more.find: Search the whole project and replace across it. The search runs in your browser tab, and your text never leaves it.
more.goal: A word goal for the book, and its shape drawn Part by Part as it grows.

organise.title: Then, the whole book.
organise.problem: A novel grows. And changes order.
organise.answer: Move a chapter and the rest of the book falls into place. Change the shape as often as the story does.

more.rule: The Golden Rule: a Part holds Parts or Sections, never both, so the shape of a project stays clear.
more.move: Drag a Section where it belongs, or select several and move them together.
more.wizard: A new project starts from a structure of your choice, with its genre, already laid out in Parts.

help.title: An AI editorial team for the whole book.
help.problem: A paragraph isn't enough. Your problems live across three hundred pages.
help.answer: It finds scenes, checks them against your reference sheets and points out what doesn't add up. Then ask for an editorial letter and a plan for revision.

more.kinds: Five kinds of chat: General, Drafting, Editorial review, Alpha reader and Beta reader. Each picks its persona, its model and how creative to be, and a reader chat knows the book only up to the chapter you choose.
more.ledgers: <f>/canon</f> and <f>/continuity</f> keep ledgers of the facts that change and the things that don't add up, checked against your reference pages.
more.pages: The assistant reads the pages each job needs. A dialogue pass reads your Prose Style and the language of your world; <f>/canon</f> Mirai checks the book against her page alone; <f>/blurb</f> waits until your Back Cover is written.
more.ghosts: A review leaves its notes in the margin as suggested comments: keep the ones that help, dismiss the rest.
more.comments: Margin comments in threads you resolve when they're done, and you can call an editor into any of them.
more.checks: Ten craft detectors go through the text in your browser first, so the model starts from evidence: echoes, filter verbs, dialogue tags, sentence rhythm and more.
more.search: It can search the web, but only after you approve, or edit, the exact query.
more.models: Sign in with your {{provider}} account and pay {{provider}} for what you use, under a spending limit of $5 or less that you set. Or run a model through {{localProvider}} on your own machine, which sends nothing off it.

keep.title: Plain files. Your folder. Yours to move.
keep.problem: Your book shouldn't be locked inside someone else's app.
keep.answer: It's saved as plain Markdown, in a folder you choose, in Remote Storage, or both. Bring it in from Word; take it out as DOCX, EPUB or PDF.

more.local: Local Storage, a folder on your device; Remote Storage; or both, kept in sync.
more.offline: Lose the connection and keep writing in the open tab: changes wait in a queue, and the app tells you what isn't synced yet.
more.import: Import docx, odt, rtf, epub, Markdown, text and HTML, with chapters detected and review comments carried into the margin.
more.export: Export to DOCX, OpenDocument, PDF, RTF, EPUB, a web page, Markdown or plain text, as a book, a manuscript or a review copy.
more.open: Free software under the AGPL: read the code, run it yourself.

revise.title: … what if the best sentence was in yesterday's version?
revise.problem: You rewrite chapter 12 and lose the line that worked.
revise.answer: Keep your drafts as snapshots. Compare any two, down to a single word, and take back only what you want.

more.history: The revision rail lets you walk back through undo history and return to an earlier version of the text.
more.snapshots: Keep drafts as snapshots and compare any two, in either direction.

keys.title: Keys that keep you writing
keys.body: Guillemets, curly quotes, the em dash, the ellipsis and the curly apostrophe are one keystroke each. So are the accented capitals an Italian keyboard can't type. No menu, no symbol picker, no break in the sentence.

henosis.title: <f>Henosis</f>: only the page
henosis.body: Write for a few seconds and the controls fade away; stop, and they come back. You decide how long each one takes.
henosis.alt: Henosis as it happens: the controls fade while you write, until only the page is left.

desk.title: The Desk: where you left off
desk.body: Open a book and its <f>Desk</f> shows the last lines you wrote, one button to carry on, the shape of every Part, and how far you've come lately.
desk.alt: The Desk: the last lines written, Continue writing, and the shape of each Part.

compare.title: Two drafts, one better book
compare.body: Compare saved drafts by paragraph, sentence or word. Accept one change at a time to keep the best of both.
compare.alt: The compare view at word level: the page's words struck through, the snapshot's words beside them.

summaries.title: A summary for every Section
summaries.body: Ask for a summary of any Section. Each one remembers the text it summed up, so when you rewrite, it is marked outdated, and one click writes it again. Summaries are how <f>/where</f> finds a scene from a description and <f>/map</f> places every Part.
summaries.alt: A Section's summary in the Summaries shelf, beside the page.

ask.title: Ask in the margin
ask.body: Write @Nova, or any editor's name, in a margin comment, and the answer arrives in that thread, about that very passage. No chat to open, no page to leave.
ask.alt: A margin thread: the writer asks @Spark about a line, and Spark answers in the thread.

autosave.title: Autosave at your pace
autosave.body: Autosave is on from the start, every thirty seconds; set the pace from every five seconds to every five minutes, or turn it off. A mark beside each paragraph shows what isn't on disk yet, and the save chip tells you when it's saving, syncing to Remote Storage, and saved.

sync.title: Two copies, one clear choice
sync.body: When your device and Remote Storage disagree, you choose which version wins, and the other is backed up first. If some of your work exists only on this device, the app tells you.

move.title: Move in, move out
move.body: Import DOCX, ODT, RTF, EPUB, Markdown, text and HTML, with chapter detection and review comments. Export to DOCX, ODT, PDF, RTF, EPUB, HTML, Markdown or text, in book, manuscript or review-copy layouts.

focus.title: The sentence you are writing, in focus
focus.body: <f>Focus</f> dims the text around your current line or paragraph. The surrounding words stay in place while the current passage takes the foreground.

structure.title: The structure follows the story
structure.body: Select Sections, move them together and group them in Parts. On a phone, move controls replace dragging.
structure.alt: Moving two Sections at once: tick them, choose Move…, then pick where they go.

templates.title: Reference sheets ask the right questions.
templates.lede: A wound from the past, a desire, a rule of your world. Each sheet asks what a good editor would ask, and leaves room for what you haven't decided yet.
templates.switch: Any page can be kept from the assistant with one switch, in every chat.
templates.details: The <f>Guidebook</f> has fourteen sections. There are also fifteen worldbuilding templates, character sheets and character arcs, in English and Italian. Each field includes craft guidance to help you develop your answer.

team.title: The same passage. Four different readings.
team.lede: Phos sees the whole book. Nova works line by line. Spark asks what the story needs next. Lumi, the beta reader, tells you where a reader would put the book down. Pick one, and what they look for.

phos.line: “Respectfully: the book promises a change of sight. First, the voice keeps that promise. Second, the people arrive too late to share it.”

nova.line: “Three sentences, one rhythm. In the first paragraph that's a choice; by the third it's an echo.”

spark.line: “This is it, this is the engine! The light spreads, therefore someone has to pay for it. But who?”

lumi.line: “I stayed up for Mirai. When she asked about the dog I actually put the book down for a second.”

commands.title: Type <f>/</f> and pick the job.
commands.lede: Check continuity, tighten a line, plan a scene, or ask for the letter.

letter.title: Feedback becomes a plan.
letter.lede: Phos writes you an editorial letter: what works, what doesn't yet, quoting your own pages. Every point becomes a task: Must, Should or Could. Tick them off as you revise.

letter.title: The letter.
letter.body: What the book is, what works and what doesn't yet, argued from your own pages and quoting them.

plan.title: The revision plan.
plan.body: Every point becomes an item, Must, Should or Could, to tick off as you revise.

draft.title: Draft this.
draft.body: Takes an item to a new drafting chat, so the plan turns into pages. What reaches the book is up to you.

followup.title: The plan follows your rewrites.
followup.body: Ask for another reading: each item is assessed as resolved, still open or made worse. Pick up with what remains to be done.

mobile.lede: On your home network, while your computer is on, open your novel on a phone or tablet, with the controls within your thumb's reach. Away from home, a tab that is already open keeps writing, and the changes wait until you are back.

free.title: Open source, all of it.
free.lede: Run your own copy: the code is open under the AGPL, with nothing held back, and you build it yourself. The AI is optional, and you pay {{provider}} for what you use.

wear.title: Pick a theme. Watch what happens.
wear.lede: Four themes, each in light and dark. Pick one and this whole page changes with it.

maker.one: I've always believed the best work happens when things that seem opposed work as one. Logic and intuition. Discipline and creativity.
maker.two: In 1997, in a maths class, I wrote my first lines of code on a sheet of paper: a Battleship game in Turbo Pascal 7. I had no computer at home, so I couldn't wait to reach the computer lab and see if it ran. Programming and play. Maths and fun.
maker.three: Today the opposites are code and writing. I was looking for software that let me work the way I wanted, and couldn't find it. So I started building it. At first it was only for me; then I thought it would be good to share it with anyone who writes and doesn't mind running a few commands to set it up.
maker.four: Bringing a little light where there was dark: that's where the name comes from. To me it means understanding a little more, learning to listen, watching something beautiful take shape.
maker.five: There is a second reason. I wanted to see how far a software project made with AI could go, without writing the code myself. So I say it plainly: the ideas, the design decisions, the testing and the debugging are mine; AI agents write the code. It is a personal project, made in my free time, with no company behind it.

demo.q: Can I try it first, to see what it's like?
demo.a: Yes. The demo is the whole editor, open on a sample novel, and it needs no account. Nothing is saved: a reload starts the novel over. The assistant answers with sample replies; to use a real model, build the program on your computer and connect your {{provider}} account, or a local model through {{localProvider}}.

files.a: In a folder on your device, in your Remote Storage, or both: plain Markdown, YAML and JSON that any editor can open. Your preferences, your <f>Library</f> and what each project card shows, such as titles, word counts and the shape of the structure, stay on your device and, while Remote Storage is connected, also in the folder reserved for the application in your Remote Storage. That folder never holds body text, snapshots, comments or chats.

cost.a: {{product}} is free software: there is nothing to buy. The AI isn't included: to use a remote model, you sign in with your {{provider}} account and pay {{provider}} for what you use, under a spending limit of $5 or less that you set. Or run a local model through {{localProvider}} on your computer, with no provider to pay.

ai.q: Which AI does it use, and what does it see?
ai.a: The model you choose. With a remote model, the passages you ask about go from your device straight to your model provider and on to the model's vendor; no central server sits in between. A model running through {{localProvider}} sends nothing off your machine, apart from a web search you approve, and then only that query. The assistant suggests changes and does not edit your manuscript; you choose which suggestions to use.

leave.q: Can I move to another program?
leave.a: Yes. Your book is already plain files, and it exports to DOCX, OpenDocument, PDF, RTF, EPUB, a web page, Markdown and plain text.

offline.a: Yes. The program starts on your computer with no connection, and books in a folder there need none. Signing in needs one, and changes to books in Remote Storage wait in a queue until you're back online.

browsers.q: Which browsers does it work in?
browsers.a: Folders on your device need a Chromium browser, such as Chrome or Edge. Remote Storage and the demo work in every modern browser.

host.a: Yes, that's how it works: {{product}} runs on your computer. You build it from the source code, then install and set it up yourself. There are no central servers.

finished.a: It's in alpha and changes fast: if you use it now, you are experimenting with something that is still being made. Every change passes the full test suite and a run in a real browser, and I review it before it's merged. Keep your own copy of anything you can't afford to lose.

demo.title: The whole editor. One click. No account.
demo.lede: The demo is the full editor, open on a sample novel: write, move chapters, compare drafts, open the reference sheets. You can't break anything: reload, and the novel is back as it was.

storage.browsers: Use a folder on your device, Remote Storage, or both. Device folders require Chrome, Edge or another Chromium browser. Remote Storage and the demo work in every modern browser. The program starts with no connection; signing in and Remote Storage need one, and if you lose it, keep writing in the open tab.

focus.hint: Pick Ln for the line or ¶ for the paragraph, then click in the text.
focus.p1: Small acts, yes. Tiny sparks that no one noticed. But each one kindled a flame. And that light grew brighter only when it was shared.
focus.p2: Over time, people began to understand something simple. Every sentient being experiences the world from its own center. A child feels joy no less than an old person. A dog hopes to return home. An elephant mourns its dead.
focus.p3: No law commanded it. No prophet carried it from town to town. It moved the way warmth moves through a room, from one body to the next, until no one could say where it had begun.

shapeDesc.empty: Nothing is laid out in advance — no Parts are created, and no shape is chosen for you.
shapeDesc.threeact: Three Acts splits a story into Setup, Confrontation and Resolution: the world as it was, the trouble that breaks it, and how it settles again.
shapeDesc.kishotenketsu: Kishōtenketsu comes from East Asian tradition and builds a story in four acts: Ki (introduction), Sho (development), Ten (twist) and Ketsu (conclusion). It turns on the twist, not on a central conflict: Ten recasts what came before, and Ketsu reconciles the two.
shapeDesc.freytagspyramid: Freytag's Pyramid stretches a dramatic arc across five Parts: Exposition, Rising action, Climax, Falling action and Denouement.
shapeDesc.herosjourney: The Hero's Journey follows someone out of their ordinary world, through trials that change them, and back home a different person: Departure, Initiation and Return.

shapeFit.empty: Start from a blank page and let the project find its own.
shapeFit.threeact: A dependable scaffold for a plot-driven novel — and an easy first structure if you have never used one.
shapeFit.freytagspyramid: A map for stories with one great peak of tension — mysteries and dramas wear it well.
shapeFit.herosjourney: A natural fit for adventure and fantasy told over one full arc.

demoModel.reply1: The opening moves quickly, and that suits it. The second paragraph stops to describe the room, though, and the tension you built drops for a while. Try keeping one detail the character would actually notice, and let the rest come out later through what they do.
demoModel.reply2: The dialogue works best where the characters say less than they mean. In the middle exchange both of them explain their feelings outright. Let one of them dodge the question, and the scene will carry more weight.
demoModel.reply3: A continuity question: in an earlier chapter the letter arrives on a Tuesday, but here the character remembers reading it at the weekend. If the change is intended, one line acknowledging it will help the reader; if not, it is an easy fix.
demoModel.reply4: As a reader, I wanted to keep going. The narrator's voice is distinct, and the last line of the section lands well. The only moment I lost my footing was the jump between the two timelines: a clearer anchor at the start of the flashback would keep me with you.
demoModel.reply5: A small line edit: “She slowly walked towards the door, feeling very nervous” could become “She edged towards the door.” The verb carries both the slowness and the nerves, and the sentence gets out of the scene's way.
demoModel.disclaimer: This is a static reply, shown only to demonstrate how the chat works: no real AI provider is available in the demo.

Signing in with {{identity}} identifies you as a writer and is required if you want to connect Remote Storage. Connecting it is a separate choice. The demo requires no account.

retention.title: How long it is kept

list.account: Your local account, preferences, library and connections stay in your browser until you remove them. When signing out, you can keep your local data or choose to clear it.
list.sessions: Your browser remembers that you are signed in until you sign out. The session cookie expires after 30 days. If you are still signed in then, the identity service makes a new one.
list.removed: Projects removed from the Library: their card goes at once. The program records the removal in the library data associated with your local account so the project does not reappear after synchronization.
list.aiKey: The {{ai}} key stays in memory until you close the tab or sign out. If you choose to have it remembered, the key is saved, encrypted, in a cookie: see the lifetimes under “Cookies and browser storage”.
list.sync: Copies of your preferences and library stay in Remote Storage after you sign out. The program can recover them when you reconnect the same storage.
list.log: The program removes log lines older than 14 days while it runs or, if it was closed, at its next start. If you choose to clear this browser when you sign out, or delete your account, the program empties the log in this browser. In the desktop app, “Wipe every configuration” empties its log files. If the desktop app stops because of an error, the file that describes the error stays on the computer, complete, until you start the app again; the program then copies it into the log without personal data and empties it.

retention.deletion: When you disconnect Remote Storage, the program asks you from where. If you disconnect it from this browser only, other devices stay connected. If you disconnect it everywhere, the program asks {{identity}} to revoke access. In the same window you can also have the remote copies of your preferences and library removed.
retention.cleanup: Before signing you out, the program saves open work and warns you if changes are still waiting to sync. If you choose to clear this browser, the program tries to remove the account’s local data and credentials. Sign-out may complete if the browser fails to remove some local data.
retention.deleteAccount: Choose “Delete your account” in Settings to remove your account from this browser. If Remote Storage is connected, the program first deletes the remote copies of your preferences and library and asks {{identity}} to revoke access. If something fails, deletion stops. The program tells you what it has already deleted and what is still there. You can try again. Your books stay in the folders you chose.
retention.revoke: Account deletion continues if {{identity}} does not confirm revocation. In that case, remove the program’s access from your {{identity}} account. To revoke your {{ai}} key, use your account with that service. Clearing the cookie does not revoke the key.

recipients.title: Who receives it

list.identity: {{identity}} handles sign-in and, if you connect it, Remote Storage, through the {{identity}} Cloud project of your installation. Sign-in asks only for your basic profile (openid, email and profile); connecting Remote Storage asks for access to the files the program creates or opens and to a folder reserved for the application, never to the rest of your storage. Your profile picture also comes from {{identity}}.
list.ai: {{ai}} forwards your request to the selected model provider. The request includes the text, context and necessary request metadata. The program asks {{ai}} to use only providers that say they do not store the text or use it for training. {{ai}} and the other services involved in the request may still retain data. Their privacy notices also explain how they handle searches.
list.search: {{encyclopedia}} receives the query you approve and connection metadata. Search through {{ai}} sends the query and a fixed instruction to the model provider. {{ai}} runs the search with {{webSearch}}, a web search engine. The model may rephrase the query sent to {{webSearch}}. The search request does not include your manuscript.
list.home: If you set up access over your home network, {{homeDns}} receives the domain name you chose and the computer’s address on that network, which it publishes in the DNS. If you create an account during setup, it also receives your email address and password. {{certificates}} receives the domain name to issue its certificate. The name appears in public Certificate Transparency logs. Both services also see the source IP address of incoming requests. {{certificates}} keeps source IP addresses. Its privacy notice gives the retention period ({{certificatesPrivacy}}).
list.updates: {{updates}} receives a request with your connection’s IP address when the library checks for a new version and when you check for updates in the desktop app. The library reuses the result for 24 hours if the browser can store it.

recipients.independent: See each provider’s privacy notice and account terms for how it handles data. Its role depends on the processing and the applicable agreements. The Author does not run these connections or receive the data exchanged through them.

transfers.title: Transfers outside the European Economic Area
transfers.body: Connected services may process data outside the European Economic Area (EEA). Countries, recipients and safeguards depend on the service, model and applicable agreements. Read the providers’ privacy notices before sending personal or confidential data. Requests go from your installation straight to these services. They do not pass through the Author, who does not receive or see them.

cookies.title: Cookies and browser storage
cookies.intro: The program uses technical cookies to keep the session open and to complete {{identity}} sign-in or the connection to Remote Storage in the same browser. A persistent cookie maintains the Remote Storage connection. If you choose to save your {{ai}} key, another cookie stores it in encrypted form. Article 5(3) of Directive 2002/58/EC and, in Italy, Article 122 of the Personal Data Protection Code (Legislative Decree 196/2003) do not require consent where storage is strictly necessary to provide a feature you explicitly request. The program does not use tracking cookies. External providers describe their own cookies in their privacy notices.

session.name: {{sessionCookie}}
session.purpose: Linking the active local account to the connections and credentials the identity service manages
session.lifetime: 30 days, or until you sign out

signIn.name: {{flowCookie}}
signIn.purpose: Keeping the authorization details in encrypted form and completing {{identity}} sign-in or the Remote Storage connection in the browser that started it

storageConnect.name: {{connectionCookie}}
storageConnect.purpose: Keeping the encrypted credential for access to Remote Storage
storageConnect.lifetime: Until you disconnect, at most 400 days

aiKey.name: {{keyCookie}}
aiKey.purpose: Keeping your {{ai}} key in encrypted form if you chose to keep it
aiKey.lifetime: Until you disconnect it or sign out cleaning the browser, at most 400 days

cookies.device: Your browser keeps the local account, preferences, library, working copies of remote files and changes waiting to be saved. The update check record and the version whose notice you dismissed are shared by the installation and stay in the browser when you delete an account. Your browser also keeps the proof that links it to its session with the identity service, your choice to keep the {{ai}} key, the theme last used and the address of your local AI models. It also keeps the program’s log and, when you close a tab, the few lines not yet written to it, until the program next starts. The log stays in this browser, and nobody reads it from elsewhere.

rights.title: Who to contact about your data
rights.body: To erase the data in your installation, choose to clear this browser when signing out or choose “Delete your account” in Settings. To erase the desktop app’s log, close the app and delete the files in its log folder (“Show the files” on the setup page), or use “Wipe every configuration”. For data handled by connected services, use your account controls or the contact details in their privacy notices. If you use a copy of {{product}} that someone else installed and runs, contact that person. The Author does not receive manuscripts or account data from the program, and so cannot provide, correct or erase them.
rights.delete: If you write to the Author at {{privacyContact}}, the website’s privacy notice applies to your messages. Do not include personal data beyond what a reply needs, or credentials, manuscripts or other people’s data. If you send the Author a log to report a problem, the Author uses it only to find the cause of the problem and deletes it when the problem is closed.
rights.complaint: If you believe that whoever processes your data infringes the GDPR, you can lodge a complaint with the competent supervisory authority. In Italy, you can contact the Garante per la protezione dei dati personali ({{supervisor}}).

automated.title: Automated decisions
automated.body: The Author and the program do not use your data to analyse or predict your behaviour, interests or habits (profiling). No automated system makes decisions that produce legal effects concerning you or similarly significantly affect you (Article 22 of the GDPR).

account.title: Local account and {{identity}} sign-in
account.body: You can use the program without a {{identity}} account. Your browser keeps a local account either way. Signing in with {{identity}} does not encrypt files on your device.
account.storage: To use Remote Storage, sign in with {{identity}} and authorize the connection. Both steps use the {{identity}} Cloud project configured for your installation. The program uses Remote Storage to sync your preferences and library across installations.

free.body: The Author distributes the program free of charge. If you use remote AI features, {{ai}} charges you under your account terms.

writing.title: Your writing
writing.body: The program does not send your writing to the Author. Using the program gives the Author no rights in what you write. The law and third-party rights also apply to material produced with AI or imported from elsewhere. With “Import” you can bring files such as documents and EPUBs into the program. If a file holds someone else’s work, import it only if the law permits it or you have the rights holder’s permission.

use.body: The licence allows you to run the program. If you modify the program and let other people use it over a network, the licence requires you to offer them the source code of your version (section 13). If you distribute the program, modified or not, you must do so under the licence and make the source code available. When accessing someone else’s writing, files or accounts, follow the law and the terms of the services you use.

warranty.title: Warranty and liability
warranty.body: The licence and the legal notice describe the exclusions of warranty and limitations of liability. Written agreements, liability for wilful misconduct or gross negligence, and other mandatory protections still apply. Keep backup copies of your writing.

aiKey.title: Your {{ai}} key
aiKey.body: To connect {{ai}}, you need a key with a spending limit set at the service. Your browser keeps the key in the tab’s memory and uses it to authenticate requests to {{ai}}. If you choose to save it, your installation’s identity service encrypts it and stores it in a cookie. Anyone with access to your browser profile while the program is open can use the saved key.
aiKey.spending: A daily, weekly or monthly spending limit resets at the start of each period. Charges billed to your own provider keys count towards the limit only if you enable that option at {{ai}}.
aiKey.revocation: You can revoke the key in your {{ai}} account. Your account terms govern charges. The Author does not receive these payments and does not refund them. For damages, the limitation of liability in the legal notice applies.

suspension.title: Releases and support
suspension.body: The Author may change the program, or stop publishing releases and updates, in whole or in part, at any time and without notice, and owes no support. The licence lets you keep and run the versions you have.

controller.title: Who publishes this site
controller.body: {{publisherName}} (the Author) publishes this static site on {{host}} Pages. The site has no accounts or forms. The Author is the controller for two activities: the publication of the site through {{host}}, which receives the technical data of your visit, and the handling of the messages the Author receives. {{host}} processes the access logs described in the next section for its own purposes, as an independent controller. The Author has no access to those logs.

logs.title: The host's access logs
logs.body: To show you a page, your browser connects to {{host}}, which receives your IP address and the technical data of the request. The Author chose this service to make the site available: the legal basis is the Author’s legitimate interest in publishing it (Article 6(1)(f) of Regulation (EU) 2016/679, the GDPR). {{host}} logs and stores your IP address to protect its service, whether or not you are signed in to {{host}}.
logs.basis: {{host}} explains its legitimate interest in security and the criteria it uses to decide how long to keep data in its privacy notice: {{hostPrivacy}}.

browser.title: Your browser
browser.body: The site sets no cookies and uses no persistent browser storage. It uses tab session storage to remember that you have seen how to leave the demo, restore scroll positions and manage reloads after an error. This data stays in the browser for the tab session. Theme and language choices stay in the open page’s memory.

notCollected.title: What the site does not do
notCollected.body: The site has no analytics, advertising, tracking or profiling integrations. It serves its own fonts and images. Your writing and requests to the demo assistant stay in the browser. No automated system makes decisions that produce legal effects concerning you or similarly significantly affect you (Article 22 of the GDPR).

transfers.title: Transfers outside the European Economic Area
transfers.body: Your visit sends technical data to {{host}} in the United States, on the basis of the adequacy decision for the EU–U.S. Data Privacy Framework. {{host}} says it processes data in the United States and other countries. Its privacy notice describes the EU–U.S. Data Privacy Framework for transfers covered by its certification. It generally uses the European Commission’s standard contractual clauses for transfers to countries without an adequacy decision. Read its privacy notice at {{hostPrivacy}}. For messages to the Author, {{mail}} keeps the mailbox in Switzerland, a country covered by an adequacy decision of the European Commission.

rights.title: Your rights
rights.body: For the access logs, you can use the contact details in {{host}}’s privacy notice. For requests about data the Author handles, use the address in the section “Messages to the Author”. Where the GDPR provides for it, you can request access, rectification, erasure, restriction or portability and object to processing.
rights.complaint: If you believe processing infringes the GDPR, you can lodge a complaint with the competent supervisory authority. In Italy, you can contact the Garante per la protezione dei dati personali ({{supervisor}}).

changes.title: Changes
changes.body: The date at the top shows when this notice was updated. Changes to the processing described here will be published on this page before they apply.

objection.title: Right to object
objection.body: This right covers the processing the Author does on the basis of legitimate interest: the publication of the site through {{host}} and the personal data in the messages you send to the Author, including messages that report a problem. You can object at any time, on grounds relating to your particular situation: write to {{privacyContact}}. The Author then stops handling that data, unless the Author shows compelling legitimate grounds that override your interests, rights and freedoms, or the data is needed to establish, exercise or defend legal claims. The objection does not cover data the Author handles to comply with a legal obligation, for example to answer a request to exercise rights under the GDPR. The Author keeps no data from your visit. For the access logs that {{host}} handles, contact {{host}}: the Author has no access to those logs.

contact.title: Messages to the Author
contact.body: You can write to the Author at {{privacyContact}}. The Author uses your email address and the information you send to handle your request. Do not include personal data beyond what a reply needs, or credentials, manuscripts or other people’s data. For general requests the legal basis is the legitimate interest in replying (Article 6(1)(f) GDPR). For requests to exercise your rights under the GDPR, it is compliance with a legal obligation (Article 6(1)(c)).
contact.optional: Writing to the Author is your choice: no law and no contract requires it. Without your email address and the information that is needed, the Author cannot reply to you.
contact.provider: {{mail}}, a company in Switzerland, provides the Author’s mailbox and processes the messages on the Author’s behalf, as a processor (Article 28 GDPR).
contact.retention: The Author keeps messages for as long as needed to handle the request and, where necessary, meet legal obligations or protect legal rights. A log you send to report a problem is used only to find its cause and is deleted when the problem is closed.
